claim: Every reflexive, transitive, time-orientation-preserving Minkowski-invariant relation containing some nonzero past causal pair equals causal past.
witness: The universal relation R(a,b)=true satisfies every listed premise but also relates future and spacelike pairs.
missing_or_conflated: A nonuniversality/unsettled-points condition is absent from this isolated statement.
permitted_conclusion: The isolated implication is false. This does not identify whether an original paper, an OCR transcription, or extraction omitted context.

claim: Adding nonuniversality to the preceding claim suffices to force inclusion of every past null pair.
witness: Let R(a,b) hold iff a=b or b is strictly timelike past of a. It is reflexive, transitive, nonuniversal and invariant under time-orientation-preserving Minkowski automorphisms, and contains past timelike pairs. In coordinates (time,space), R((0,0),(-1,1)) is false because that displacement is null.
missing_or_conflated: Containing one past timelike pair does not imply containing the whole causal past; a condition supplying null inclusion or an appropriate closure assumption is needed.
permitted_conclusion: This refutes the weakened statement only, not a reconstruction that explicitly assumes all causal-past pairs are included.

claim: A nonzero finite-dimensional complex clock admits matrices T,H with TH-HT=i*hbar*I for nonzero real hbar.
witness: Trace cyclicity gives tr(TH-HT)=0. The asserted right side has trace i*hbar*n, which is nonzero when n is a positive integer and hbar is nonzero.
missing_or_conflated: An exact ideal canonical clock algebra was silently transferred into a nonzero finite-dimensional model.
permitted_conclusion: The exact matrix commutator is impossible. Periodic clocks, POVM clocks and approximate clock relations are not ruled out.

claim: Normalizing any completely positive trace-nonincreasing instrument outcome gives a linear trace-preserving quantum channel on all input states.
witness: For K=diag(1,1/sqrt(2)), use J(rho)=K*rho*K*. Each computational-basis pure state is unchanged by normalized J, but the equal mixture is mapped to diag(2/3,1/3), not the equal mixture of the two normalized outputs.
missing_or_conflated: A subnormalized linear instrument is different from its normalized conditional state update. The outcome probability can depend on the input.
permitted_conclusion: This explicit normalized update is not affine. Do not infer a universal iff characterization from this example or apply channel criteria before defining the appropriate map.

claim: A continuous quantum evolution that fails the homogeneous semigroup law must fail complete-positive divisibility.
witness: For t>=0, let a qubit dephasing channel multiply off-diagonal entries by exp(-t^2/2). The propagator from s to t has factor exp(-(t^2-s^2)/2) in (0,1] for t>=s, so is CPTP. Yet exp(-(s+t)^2/2) differs from exp(-(s^2+t^2)/2) when s,t>0.
missing_or_conflated: Time-homogeneous semigroup evolution, CP divisibility, and multi-time process memory are distinct criteria.
permitted_conclusion: This family is CP-divisible but not a homogeneous semigroup. No conclusion about every multi-time intervention process follows from these one-time maps alone.
